name: LMR14206XMKX_NOPB
title: 42 V input, 0.6 A step-down voltage regulator in SOT-23
summary: The LMR14206 is a PWM step-down (buck) regulator with a 0.9 Ω typical internal switch, switching at a fixed 1.25 MHz from inputs of 4.5 V to 42 V and delivering up to 0.6 A. An external divider sets the output from 0.765 V to 34 V; the power stage uses an external Schottky diode. Compensation is internal, and an RC network on the shutdown pin sets the soft-start time. It comes in a 6-pin thin SOT-23 package.

pins.name: CB
pins.function: Gate-drive supply for the internal switch. The bootstrap capacitor CBOOT goes from CB to SW.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback input, regulated to VFB. A divider from the output sets VOUT = VFB (1 + R1/R2); keep the divider resistors between 100 Ω and 10 kΩ so the FB bias current adds little error.

pins.name: SHDN
pins.function: Shutdown input, active low, logic level. Low turns the regulator off, high turns it on. Unused, it is tied to VIN or left open. Its voltage also sets the current limit during soft-start.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input, 4.5 V to 42 V in normal operation.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Output of the internal power FET; the inductor, the catch diode and CBOOT connect to it.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The basic step-down circuit. VIN feeds both the VIN and SHDN pins. SW drives inductor L1 toward the output; Schottky D1 returns the inductor current from ground when the switch opens; COUT holds the output. CBOOT between CB and SW powers the switch's gate drive. R1 and R2 divide VOUT down to FB. CIN bypasses the input.

circuits.title: Application circuit, 3.3 V output
circuits.description: A buck converter giving 3.3 V from an input of 4.5 V to 42 V. SHDN is wired to VIN. The switch on SW drives the 15 µH inductor; the 60 V, 1 A Schottky D1 carries the inductor current while the switch is off, and the 47 µF output capacitor smooths the result. CBOOT, 0.15 µF from CB to SW, supplies the switch's gate drive. R1 (3.4 kΩ) over R2 (1.02 kΩ) bring the output down to the 0.765 V that FB holds. CIN, 2.2 µF, decouples the input.

operation.text: A fixed 1.25 MHz, current-mode PWM step-down regulator with a 0.9 Ω typical internal high-side switch, internal compensation and a 0.765 V feedback reference. It runs from 4.5 V to 42 V, delivers up to 0.6 A, and sets outputs from 0.765 V to 34 V. Shutdown current is 16 µA typical; efficiency is 85 % typical.

Thermal shutdown turns the power switch off when the die gets too hot (175 °C typical, releasing at 155 °C). An input undervoltage lockout keeps the part from switching below its minimum input voltage while the supply rises and falls. A second lockout on the CB gate-drive supply holds switching off until there is enough voltage to drive the MOSFET. The output is short-circuit protected. In shutdown the supply current falls to about 16 µA.

The switch sits between VIN and SW. While it is on, the diode is reverse biased and the inductor current ramps up, feeding the load and COUT. While it is off, the inductor current keeps flowing through the now forward-biased diode into the output. When the inductor current never falls to zero, the on/off ratio sets the output voltage, VOUT ≈ D × VIN.
A resistor divider from the output to FB sets VOUT; FB regulates at 0.765 V. A starting value for R2 is 100 Ω to 10 kΩ, and R1 follows from the divider equation.

A low-ESR ceramic capacitor of 2.2 µF to 10 µF, X5R or X7R, sits between VIN and GND to keep large transients off the input. A ceramic capacitor can lose up to half its nominal capacitance at its rated voltage, so its derating with voltage and temperature counts.

The inductor is chosen on inductance, peak current and DC resistance. Inductance follows from the allowed peak-to-peak ripple current and the input and output voltages. Accepting more ripple lowers the inductance needed but adds conduction and core loss, stresses the inductor and switch, and needs more output capacitance to hold the same output ripple. A ripple target of 30 % of the DC load current is reasonable; ripple rises with VIN, so L is worked out at the maximum input voltage. A larger winding area gives lower DC resistance; sizing the core so copper loss is 2 % of output power trades efficiency against size. For most designs 10 µH to 22 µH with a current rating of 1.1 A or more is a starting point: the regulator then reaches its current limit before the inductor saturates, rather than relying on thermal shutdown and risking the inductor under a short circuit or sustained overload.
The allowed output ripple sets COUT. ESR usually dominates the ripple, so low-ESR ceramic capacitors suit the part; 22 µF to 100 µF with ESR of 0.1 Ω or less is a good place to start.
CBOOT is a ceramic capacitor of at least 0.15 µF. When VIN is under twice VOUT, a larger one, generally 0.15 µF to 1 µF, keeps the gate drive strong and RDSON consistently low.

An RC network on SHDN shapes start-up. Between 0 V and 2.3 V on SHDN, the cycle-by-cycle current limit scales from its minimum at 0 V up to the full rated limit at 2.3 V, which governs the output's rise time and the inrush current. The resistor must source more current into SHDN than the pin's 1.5 µA leakage once SHDN reaches 2.3 V or more.

SHDN accepts logic signals of 2.3 V or higher. Without shutdown control it is tied to VIN. SHDN is kept at or below 42 V; to drive it from a higher voltage, a series resistor of 100 kΩ or more between that voltage and the pin protects the part.

D1's breakdown rating should be 25 % above the highest input voltage. For best reliability its current rating equals the highest output current. Above 50 % duty cycle the average diode current falls to about (1 − D) × IOUT, so a lower average rating can serve, provided the peak rating still exceeds the largest load current. A diode rated 0.5 A to 1 A is a good start.

R1 and R2 sit next to the FB pin, away from the inductor, and the divider's ground goes straight to the GND pin on a dedicated trace, limiting conducted noise pick-up. CIN goes close to the VIN pin, which keeps trace resistance from adding input ripple. L1 goes close to SW to limit EMI and capacitive coupling. COUT sits near where L1 and D1 join, and the L1, D1 and COUT traces are kept short to reduce conducted and radiated noise and improve efficiency. The ground connections of D1, CIN and COUT are kept small and meet the system ground plane at one point, preferably COUT's ground.
The built-in ESD protection is limited. Store and handle the part with its leads shorted together or in conductive foam so the MOS gates are not damaged.
